analysis: The supplied units are base-side excerpts (lines 37889-39600) of fixtures/prompt-contract/v1/production_vectors.json, a public synthetic golden-vector file. They contain gpt-oss-20b chat_completions vectors (multi_system, nulls, reasoning_effort, response_text) with request_body, provider_body, template_input, plan (prompt_contract_id, block_boundaries, chain hashes) and token_ids. The content is public placeholder text (e.g. 'Public followup.', 'Public synthetic cache-parity input.'), and I saw no secrets, keys, tokens or real consumer data. The PR patch, partially visible, only changes fixture data: it adds additional_context enable_thinking=false to a template_input and changes prompt_token_count, chain hashes and token_ids for a Qwen-style vector near base line 3017-3082, along with other fixture edits at roughly base lines 43813 and 52418. No executable code, authorization, attestation, encryption, or routing logic is modified in the supplied material. The prefix-cache chain hashes (T-041) are public test vectors, so changing them does not weaken the at-rest HMAC-keyed cache design. Remaining questions for integration: the head-side values and the other changed ranges were not visible in these units. Whether the fixtures are consistent with the Swift/Go prompt-contract implementation (template rendering, enable_thinking handling, block hashing) cannot be verified here. A mismatch would be a correctness and cache-parity risk rather than a demonstrated security regression. I make no claim about cross-tenant cache-sharing semantics beyond the fixtures.
